item.title: How LeetCode Drills and the Front-End/Back-End Split Damaged a Generation of Chinese Programmers
item.description: In the age of AI, is drilling interview trivia and carving yourself into a fixed station on the front-end/back-end assembly line still necessary — or already redundant? A clear look at what those drills actually test, what AI changed, and the engineering judgment that still makes a programmer valuable.

item.title: Don't Let the AI Write Your Code: A Haskell Developer's Anti-Burnout Playbook
item.description: A 10,000-word, 100% human-written post on the Haskell Discourse blew up on HN (163 points, 216 comments). A professional Haskell developer draws a precise line through LLM-assisted development: the machine plans, researches, and reviews — you write the code. Here's the reasoning.

item.title: Some Things Just Take Time
item.description: Armin Ronacher on software development in the AI era: why a 50-year-old oak tree cannot be mass-produced, and why the things that truly matter all need time.

item.title: Rust + AI Are Quietly Killing Python's Biggest Advantage (And Most Devs Haven't Noticed)
item.description: Python didn't dominate AI because it's fast, but because it tolerates human uncertainty. But when AI starts writing code, that advantage is slowly disappearing.
